summary:
Russia launched a major overnight assault on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, killing seven people and triggering emergency power cuts in Kyiv and nearby regions. Ukraine said 11 regions were attacked, with residential buildings and railways also hit. The strikes came as officials warned of a difficult winter for the country’s energy system.

A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia after one pilot stabbed the other in the cockpit. Passengers helped restrain the attacker, and the plane landed safely after losing about 17,000 feet; the UAE is investigating whether terrorist activity was involved. Pakistan also launched airstrikes in Afghanistan, but the two governments gave conflicting accounts of the deaths: Kabul said at least nine civilians were killed, while Islamabad said 22 fighters died.

Christa Pike survived Tennessee’s attempt to execute her after two injections of pentobarbital. Governor Bill Lee halted the state’s remaining executions for the year and ordered a review. Japan raised its permanent residency fee by 20 times as part of immigration policy changes; critics say the measures could worsen labor shortages. Donald Trump announced $200 billion in planned South Korean energy investments, but Seoul said the package was far from finalised.

headlines.title: Russian strikes hit Ukraine’s energy infrastructure
headlines.summary: Russia launched a major overnight assault on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, killing seven people and prompting emergency power cuts. Ukraine said 11 regions were attacked, with residential buildings and railways also hit.

headlines.title: Flydubai flight diverted after cockpit stabbing
headlines.summary: A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia after one pilot stabbed the other, and passengers helped subdue the attacker. The plane landed safely after losing about 17,000 feet; the UAE is investigating possible terrorist activity.

headlines.title: Pakistan and Afghanistan give conflicting accounts of airstrikes
headlines.summary: Pakistan said it struck militant hideouts in Afghanistan, while the Taliban government said the attacks killed at least nine civilians. Pakistan said 22 fighters were killed in strikes on two provinces.

headlines.title: Tennessee pauses executions after failed lethal injection
headlines.summary: Christa Pike survived Tennessee’s attempt to execute her after two injections of pentobarbital. Governor Bill Lee halted the state’s remaining executions for the year and ordered a review.

headlines.title: Japan raises permanent residency fee twentyfold
headlines.summary: Japan has raised the fee for permanent residency by 20 times as part of changes to its immigration policy. Critics say the measures could worsen labor shortages.

headlines.title: South Korea says Trump’s $200 billion energy deal is not final
headlines.summary: Donald Trump announced $200 billion in planned South Korean energy investments, including funding for an Alaska liquefied natural gas project and nuclear power. Seoul said the deal is far from finalised, contradicting Trump’s presentation of the package.

headlines.title: Student protests over French schools lead to hundreds detained
headlines.summary: Student protests over teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms have escalated in France, with hundreds detained. Some demonstrations involved clashes that left dozens injured.

headlines.title: Morocco names its first woman prime minister
headlines.summary: Morocco’s king appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country’s first female prime minister. The 50-year-old lawyer and politician leads the centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party.
